stem: What is the typical dental effect of prolonged pacifier use?

options.text: Anterior open bite with the front teeth not overlapping
Premature eruption of the permanent teeth
Permanent loss of the upper central incisors
Posterior crossbite with the back teeth not touching

explanation: Anterior open bite is the typical dental effect of prolonged pacifier use. The pacifier can prevent normal overlap of the upper and lower front teeth, leaving a gap when the mouth is closed.
rationale: This describes an anterior open bite, in which the front teeth do not meet.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because prolonged pacifier use can prevent the front teeth from overlapping, producing an anterior open bite.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pacifier use may alter tooth position but does not typically make permanent teeth erupt early.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because pacifier use affects alignment rather than causing the teeth to be permanently lost.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the classic effect is an anterior open bite, not a posterior crossbite.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because pacifier use is more likely to affect incisor overlap than directly cause lower incisor crowding.

source.hint: The term for this condition describes a lack of contact between the front upper and lower teeth.
